score.finalMessage:
`daily_revenue` is fixed for every day, and 2026-09-18 now shows **$118.00 from 3 orders**, which matches your payment dashboard.

**Cause:** the SQL in `assets/daily_revenue.sql` joined each order to its line items before counting. An order with 3 line items became 3 rows, so it was counted 3 times as an order and its total was added 3 times. On 09-18, order 114 (3 items, $52) was counted three times and order 112 (2 items, $51) twice, which turned $118 into $273. Every day with multi-item orders was inflated the same way. The `items` column was already correct.

**Fix:** the asset now adds up item quantities per order first, then joins one row per order. I also changed it to a left join, so a paid order with no line items still counts toward orders and revenue instead of being dropped.

**Verified:** I rebuilt the table (`croft run daily_revenue`, both checks passed) and compared every day with totals worked out directly from `shop_orders` and `shop_order_items`. All 5 days match:

| day | orders | revenue | items |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-15 | 2 | $58.00 | 6 |
| 2026-09-16 | 2 | $72.50 | 5 |
| 2026-09-17 | 3 | $79.00 | 8 |
| 2026-09-18 | 3 | $118.00 | 12 |
| 2026-09-19 | 2 | $45.50 | 3 |

The change to `assets/daily_revenue.sql` is not committed yet, since you didn't ask for a commit.

**Needs your approval:** nothing. Rebuilding this SQL table isn't on the list of actions that need your approval, so I didn't hold anything back.

score.finalMessage:
I've added both tables and loaded them. `stripe_charges` is set to refresh every hour, but the schedule won't run until you switch scheduling on. That needs your approval, so it's the first command at the end.

**`stripe_charges`** (`assets/stripe_charges.ts`)
- It pulls charges from `STRIPE_API_BASE` in `lib/stripe.ts` using `STRIPE_KEY`. I didn't open `.env`.
- The first load brought in 207 charges (160 succeeded and kept, 21 succeeded then fully refunded, 20 failed, 6 pending), all in USD, dated 2026-08-03 to 2026-09-21.
- **Late refunds:** Stripe can only filter charges by when they were created, not when they last changed. So every run re-reads the last 180 days of charges and updates any that were refunded since. I chose 180 days because card refunds are generally allowed for about that long. A refund on a charge older than that would be missed, so shorten or lengthen the window if your refund policy differs.

**`daily_revenue`** (`assets/daily_revenue.sql`): one row per day with `day` and `revenue`.
- Revenue is successful charges minus whatever was refunded on them, converted from cents to dollars. A partial refund takes off only the refunded part.
- Days are Los Angeles days (the project's time zone), not UTC.
- A refund comes off the day the original charge was made, not the day it was refunded. That's the only way to read "charges that weren't refunded" when refunds arrive weeks later, but it means past days' revenue can go down after the fact.
- Days with no kept revenue show 0 rather than being left out. There are 50 days from 2026-08-03 to 2026-09-21, totalling $19,019.57. That matches the sum taken straight from `stripe_charges`.
- `daily_revenue` rebuilds automatically after each charges refresh.

Things revenue doesn't account for: Stripe fees are not deducted, and there are no disputes (chargebacks) in the data yet. If a chargeback happens, that charge would still count as revenue.

I haven't committed anything to git.

**Needs your approval:**
- `croft schedule on`: turns on the hourly refresh. Changing the schedule is on this project's ask-first list. The setting and the first run by hand are already done.
  - Depending on how scheduling runs here (`croft docs scheduling`), something may also need to keep running for the hourly fetches to happen. If that's `croft serve`, start it in your own terminal: it also needs your approval because it runs the scheduled work on its own.

diff --git a/assets/daily_revenue.sql b/assets/daily_revenue.sql
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..ecb916d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/assets/daily_revenue.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,26 @@
+-- description: Revenue kept per day (America/Los_Angeles): succeeded Stripe charges minus refunds, in dollars
+-- key: day
+-- check: min_rows(1)
+-- check: not_null(revenue)
+-- check: revenue >= 0
+-- A charge counts on the day it was made, in the project time zone. Refunds (full or partial) come off that
+-- charge's day via amount_refunded, which stripe_charges keeps current by re-reading recent charges every hour.
+-- Days between the first and last charge with nothing kept show 0.
+WITH kept AS (
+  SELECT
+    timezone('America/Los_Angeles', to_timestamp(created))::DATE AS day,
+    amount - amount_refunded                                      AS kept_cents
+  FROM stripe_charges
+  WHERE status = 'succeeded'
+),
+days AS (
+  SELECT unnest(generate_series(min(day), max(day), INTERVAL 1 DAY))::DATE AS day
+  FROM kept
+)
+SELECT
+  days.day,
+  CAST(coalesce(sum(kept.kept_cents), 0) / 100.0 AS DECIMAL(18, 2)) AS revenue
+FROM days
+LEFT JOIN kept USING (day)
+GROUP BY days.day
+ORDER BY days.day
diff --git a/assets/stripe_charges.ts b/assets/stripe_charges.ts
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..f2f8333
--- /dev/null
+++ b/assets/stripe_charges.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+// assets/stripe_charges.ts: Stripe charges (GET /v1/charges), newest first, paged with starting_after/has_more.
+//
+// Charges change after they are created: refunds can land weeks later and set refunded/amount_refunded. Stripe's
+// list endpoint only filters by creation time, so each run re-reads the last 180 days of charges and the key
+// merges the updated rows (Stripe card refunds are generally possible for up to ~180 days after the charge).
+import { ingest } from "@zabaca/croft";
+import { STRIPE_API_BASE } from "../lib/stripe";
+
+// The fields this code reads. The table gets every field the API returns (nested objects become JSON columns).
+type Item = { id: string; created: number };
+type Page = { data: Item[]; has_more: boolean };
+
+export default ingest({
+  description: "Stripe charges, one row per charge",
+  secrets: ["STRIPE_KEY"],
+  key: "id",
+  incremental: { field: "created", unit: "s", lookback: "180 days" },
+  schedule: "every hour",
+  checks: ["not_null(created)", "not_null(amount)", "not_null(status)"],
+
+  async *rows({ since, http, secret }) {
+    let after: string | undefined;
+    for (;;) {
+      const res = await http.get(`${STRIPE_API_BASE}/v1/charges`, {
+        headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${secret("STRIPE_KEY")}` },
+        query: { limit: 100, "created[gte]": since, starting_after: after },
+      });
+      const page = res.json<Page>();
+      yield page.data;
+      if (!page.has_more || page.data.length === 0) return;
+      after = page.data.at(-1)!.id;
+    }
+  },
+});

score.finalMessage:
The pipeline is fixed and `daily_revenue` is current again, including 2026-09-23. I checked every day in it against the raw orders and line items, and none differ.

**What went wrong**
- **Root cause:** `shop_orders` only ever fetched the first page of orders. The shop API returns 100 orders per page and says when more exist, but the ingest in `assets/shop_orders.ts` never asked for page 2. That went unnoticed while the shop had 100 orders or fewer. Yesterday orders 1101 and 1102 arrived and landed on page 2, so they were never loaded.
- **Why it failed instead of going quietly wrong:** `shop_order_items` did fetch the items for orders 1101 and 1102. Its check that every item belongs to a known order rejected them, so it wrote nothing. `daily_revenue` then skipped its rebuild and stayed frozen at the 22nd.

**What I changed** (not committed; both edits are in the working tree)
1. **`assets/shop_orders.ts`:** it now reads every page until the API reports no more. It fetched 102 orders in 2 requests.
2. **`assets/daily_revenue.sql`:** a paid order with no line items used to disappear from that day's order count and revenue. Now it still counts, with 0 items. This was already happening: order 1100 was paid but its items were in the rejected load, so it was missing from the 23rd.

**Reruns**
- `shop_orders` now has 102 rows (2 added).
- `shop_order_items` now has 179 rows (12 added). All 4 checks pass.
- `daily_revenue` now has 54 days. 2026-09-23 shows 3 paid orders, $244, 15 items. All earlier days were unchanged.
- `croft status` shows every asset ok.

2026-09-22 has no row because there were no paid orders that day, not because anything is missing.

**Needs your approval:** nothing. No step needed a `croft confirm`, and I didn't delete anything or change a schedule. Scheduling in croft is off, so I left alone whatever triggers the nightly run.

The orders pipeline runs again, and none of your existing orders were lost. `shop_orders` went from 17 rows to 22 and `daily_revenue` rebuilt with no errors.

**What broke:** API v2 sends `total_cents` as text (`"3300"`) instead of a number. The stored column is a whole number, so croft refused the load and rolled it back. Nothing was written and nothing was lost.

**The fix** (`assets/shop_orders.ts`): the code now turns `total_cents` back into a whole number as it comes in, whichever way the API sends it. If a value is ever not a plain whole number (say `"33.00"` or `"n/a"`), the run stops with a clear error rather than saving a wrong or empty amount.

**Checks on the result:**
- The run only adds new orders or updates existing ones by `id`. It added 5 orders (118–122), updated 1 and left 1 unchanged. Nothing was deleted, and the 22 order IDs are all distinct.
- Order 105 changed from pending to paid with the same $48.00 amount. That confirms v2 amounts are still in cents, so revenue isn't off by 100×.
- `daily_revenue` now covers Sept 15–21 and includes the new orders.

I didn't commit the change to git. I also didn't need to run anything that needs your approval.

**The one thing I couldn't do:** my first attempt at the edit (a `python3` script) was blocked because it needed approval. I made the same change with the file editor instead, so nothing is left to run. If you want the fix in git, run:
`git commit -am "shop_orders: accept string total_cents from API v2"`
